_about: What each Cloudflare Radar industry label covers, shown behind the info icon. Cloudflare publishes no definitions; its glossary says only that industries group businesses by their primary activities. Most labels match LinkedIn's industry list word for word, and for those the text follows LinkedIn's definition (source 'linkedin', with LinkedIn's current name where it changed). Labels with no LinkedIn match are our own reading (source 'cloudflare').

Accounting: Firms that keep the books, audit accounts, prepare tax returns and give financial advice to people and businesses.
Adult Entertainment: Websites and services that sell or host sexually explicit content for adults.
Airlines/Aviation: Airlines, airports and the companies that fly passengers or cargo, along with the businesses that support them on the ground.
Apparel & Fashion: Brands and designers that make clothing, shoes and accessories, and the shops that sell their own lines.
Architecture & Planning: Architects, landscape architects and town planners who design buildings, public spaces and the way land is used.
Arts and Crafts: Businesses that make or sell handmade goods and the materials people use for crafts and hobbies.
Automotive: Car and truck makers, the companies that supply their parts, and the dealers and garages that sell and service vehicles.
Banking: Banks and credit unions that take deposits, lend money and run accounts for people and businesses.
Biotechnology: Companies and labs that use living cells and biological processes to develop medicines, diagnostic tests and other products.
Broadcast Media: Television and radio broadcasters, including the websites and streaming services they run alongside their channels.
Broadcasting: Television and radio stations and networks that put out programmes over the air, by cable or online.
Building Materials: Companies that make or supply what buildings are made from, such as cement, timber, glass, bricks and insulation.
Business Services: Companies that sell services to other businesses, such as office support, payroll, facilities management and document handling.
Chemicals: Companies that make chemicals, whether bulk industrial chemicals or specialty products such as coatings, adhesives and fertilisers.
Civic & Social Organization: Clubs, associations and community groups that bring people together around a shared interest, cause or neighbourhood.
Commercial Real Estate: Companies that own, lease, broker or manage offices, shops, warehouses and other property used by businesses.
Computer & Network Security: Companies that make security software and hardware, or provide services that protect computer systems and networks from attack.
Computer Games: Studios and publishers that make video games for consoles, computers and phones.
Computer Hardware: Companies that make computers, servers, storage, components and peripherals such as keyboards and printers.
Computer Software: Companies that build and sell software, from desktop programs and mobile apps to the online tools businesses pay for by subscription.
Construction: Builders and contractors who put up homes, commercial buildings, roads and other infrastructure.
Consumer Electronics: Companies that make phones, televisions, headphones, cameras and other electronics people buy for their homes.
Consumer Goods: Companies that make the everyday products households buy, such as cleaning supplies, toiletries, packaged food and small appliances.
Consumer products: Brands and makers of products sold to ordinary shoppers, from household items and toiletries to small gadgets.
Consumer Services: Businesses that sell services directly to individuals, such as repairs, cleaning, personal care and other help around the home.
Cosmetics: Brands that make makeup, skincare, haircare, fragrance and other personal-care products.
Cryptocurrency: Exchanges, wallets, blockchain projects and other businesses built around digital currencies.
Design: Studios and freelancers who do graphic, product, interior or brand design for their clients.
E-Learning: Websites and companies that teach through online courses, tutoring and other digital learning tools.
Ecommerce: Online shops and marketplaces where people buy goods over the internet.
Education: Schools, colleges, universities and other organisations that teach or support learning.
Education Management: Schools and universities and the organisations that run them, including school districts and companies that provide education services.
Electrical/Electronic Manufacturing: Companies that make electrical and electronic equipment, such as motors, wiring, circuit boards and power systems.
Entertainment: Companies that produce or put on entertainment, including live shows, theme parks, studios and venues.
Environmental Services: Firms that handle waste, clean up pollution and advise organisations on their environmental impact and obligations.
Events Services: Companies that plan, host or sell tickets for conferences, weddings, concerts and other events.
Executive Office: The offices of heads of state and government, such as a president's or prime minister's office.
Farming: Farms, ranches and other producers that grow crops or raise livestock.
Finance: Banks, lenders, investment firms, payment companies and other businesses whose work is managing or moving money.
Financial Services: Companies that move, lend, invest or insure money, including payment processors, lenders, brokers and insurers.
Fine Art: Artists, galleries, auction houses and dealers that create or sell works of art.
Food & Beverages: Companies behind the food and drink brands sold in shops, cafés and restaurants.
Food Production: Manufacturers and processors that turn raw ingredients into packaged and prepared food.
Furniture: Companies that design, make or sell furniture for homes and offices.
Gambling & Casinos: Casinos, sports betting companies, lotteries and online gambling sites.
Gaming: Video game studios and publishers and the platforms where people buy, play and stream games.
Government: Government bodies at every level, from national ministries to local councils.
Government Administration: Public agencies and departments that run government services and enforce regulations.
Health, Wellness and Fitness: Gyms, personal trainers, spas, nutrition coaches and other businesses that help people stay healthy.
Higher Education: Universities, colleges and other institutions that award degrees.
Holding Companies: Companies that exist mainly to own controlling shares in other companies.
Holding Companies & Conglomerates: Holding groups and conglomerates that own a range of businesses, often in unrelated industries.
Hospital & Health Care: Hospitals, clinics, doctors' practices, care homes and other providers of medical care.
Hospitality: Hotels, holiday rentals, bars, restaurants and other businesses that look after guests.
Human Resources: Firms that handle hiring, payroll, benefits, training or HR consulting on behalf of other companies.
Industrial Automation: Companies that make the control systems, robots and sensors used to automate factories and industrial plants.
Information Services: Libraries, archives, data providers and search portals that collect information and make it available to others.
Information Technology and Services: Consultancies and service firms that design, build, run or support computer systems for other organisations.
Insurance: Insurers, brokers and agents who sell cover for health, life, property, vehicles and businesses.
International Affairs: International organisations, embassies and diplomatic bodies that work on relations between countries.
International Trade and Development: Import and export businesses, trade promotion bodies and organisations that fund or run development programmes abroad.
Internet: Companies whose main product is a website or online service, such as search engines, social networks, marketplaces, streaming services and web hosts.
Internet Service Providers, Website Host: Companies that sell internet access, host websites or provide the domains and other services needed to put a site online.
Investment Banking: Banks and advisory firms that help companies raise money and buy, sell or merge businesses.
Investment Management: Asset managers, fund companies and wealth managers who invest money on behalf of their clients.
IT Services: Companies that set up, run and support computer systems, networks and software for their clients.
Law Enforcement: Police forces and other agencies whose job is enforcing the law.
Law Practice: Law firms and lawyers who represent and advise clients.
Legal Services: Providers of legal help outside law firms, such as notaries, paralegals, legal publishers and online legal services.
Leisure, Travel & Tourism: Travel agencies, booking sites, tour operators and the attractions tourists visit.
Libraries: Public, academic and specialist libraries and the archives that keep records and collections.
Local Business: Small businesses that serve one town or area, such as shops, tradespeople and local service providers.
Logistics and Supply Chain: Companies that move and store goods, including freight forwarders, couriers, shipping lines and warehouses.
Luxury Goods & Jewelry: Luxury brands and jewellers selling high-end watches, jewellery, leather goods and similar items.
Machinery: Companies that make industrial machines such as engines, pumps and tools, and equipment for farms and building sites.
Management Consulting: Consultancies that advise organisations on strategy, operations, finance and how they are run.
Manufacturing: Companies that make physical products in factories, across many different kinds of goods.
Market Research: Firms that run surveys and studies on markets, customers and public opinion, and sell what they find.
Marketing and Advertising: Ad agencies, marketing firms and companies that buy, sell or place advertising.
Mechanical or Industrial Engineering: Engineering firms that design machines, production lines and industrial processes.
Media: Companies that produce or publish news, entertainment and other content in print, on air or online.
Media & Internet: Publishers, broadcasters and online platforms that make content or distribute it on the web.
Media Production: Studios and production companies that make video, audio, animation and other content, usually for clients.
Medical Devices: Companies that make medical equipment, from surgical instruments and implants to scanners and patient monitors.
Military: Armed forces and defence ministries and the bodies that run them.
Mining & Metals: Companies that mine coal, metals and minerals or process metals such as steel and aluminium.
Motion Pictures and Film: Film studios, producers and distributors that make and release movies.
Museums and Institutions: Museums, historic sites, zoos and other cultural institutions open to the public.
Music: Record labels, music publishers, artists and the businesses around recorded and live music.
Newspapers: Publishers of daily and weekly newspapers, in print and online.
Non-Profit: Charities, foundations and other nonprofit organisations working for a cause.
Nonprofit Organization Management: Charities, foundations and other nonprofits, along with the organisations that manage and fund them.
Oil & Energy: Companies that produce, refine or sell oil, gas, coal and other forms of energy, including renewables.
Online Media: Publishers and creators that release audio and video only on the internet, such as podcasts and online video channels.
Organizations: Associations, societies and membership bodies that are not run as businesses.
Outsourcing/Offshoring: Companies that take on work for other businesses, often from another country, such as customer support, back-office tasks and software development.
Paper & Forest Products: Companies that manage forests and turn wood into timber, pulp, paper and packaging.
Performing Arts: Theatre, dance, opera and music companies and the venues where they perform.
Pharmaceuticals: Companies that research, make and sell medicines.
Photography: Photographers, photo studios and stock-image businesses.
Plastics: Manufacturers of plastic materials and plastic products such as packaging, pipes, film and moulded parts.
Political Organization: Political parties, campaigns and advocacy groups that work to influence elections and policy.
Print & Digital Media: Publishers of magazines, newspapers and books that release their work both in print and online.
Printing: Commercial printers that produce books, packaging, labels, signs and marketing materials for clients.
Professional Training & Coaching: Trainers, coaches and course providers who help working professionals build their skills.
Professional Training; Corporate: Companies that run training programmes for employers and their staff.
Public Policy: Think tanks, policy institutes and public bodies that research and shape government policy.
Public Relations and Communications: PR agencies and communications consultancies that manage how organisations deal with the press and the public.
Publishing: Publishers of books, magazines, journals and other periodicals, in print and online.
Real Estate: Estate agents, brokers, landlords and property managers dealing in homes and other property.
Recreational Facilities and Services: Leisure centres, golf courses, ski resorts, parks and other places people go for recreation.
Religious Institutions: Churches, mosques, temples, synagogues and other religious organisations.
Research: Research institutes, labs and firms that carry out scientific, technical or social research.
Restaurants: Restaurants, cafés, takeaways and food delivery businesses.
Retail: Shops and chains that sell goods to the public, in stores or online.
Security and Investigations: Companies that provide security guards, alarm monitoring, private investigation and similar protection services.
Semiconductors: Companies that design or manufacture computer chips, and the makers of the equipment used to produce them.
software: Companies that build and sell software, including apps and the subscription services businesses run on.
Sporting Goods: Companies that make or sell sports equipment, sportswear and outdoor gear.
Sports: Professional and amateur sports teams, leagues, clubs and governing bodies.
Staffing and Recruiting: Recruitment agencies, staffing firms and job boards that match people with jobs.
Supermarkets: Supermarket and grocery chains, including their online shopping and delivery services.
Telecommunications: Companies that provide phone, mobile, cable, satellite and internet connections.
Think Tanks: Independent institutes that research policy, economic and social questions and publish their findings to influence public debate.
Translation and Localization: Translators and agencies that adapt text, websites and software for other languages and markets.
Transportation/Trucking/Railroad: Trucking companies, railways, bus operators and other businesses that carry goods or people over land.
US Federal Government: Departments and agencies of the United States federal government.
US State Government: Agencies and departments run by the individual US state governments.
Utilities: Companies that supply electricity, gas, water and sewage services.
Veterinary: Vets, animal hospitals and other providers of care for pets and livestock.
Website Design & Managment: Agencies and freelancers who design, build and maintain websites for clients.
Wholesale: Wholesalers and distributors that buy goods in bulk from manufacturers and sell them on to shops and other businesses.
Wine and Spirits: Wineries, breweries, distillers and the brands and merchants that sell alcoholic drinks.
Writing and Editing: Writers, editors, copywriters and agencies that produce or polish written content for clients.
